stories.title: generate-icons: Agent skill that draws an original icon library matching your design system (React, Vue, Svelte, React Native, SVG)
stories.body:
An agent skill that draws an original icon library that matches your project's design system.

It reads your tokens, theme, fonts and the icons you already use, turns that into an explicit style sheet, proves it on a small sample shown next to your real UI, and only then draws the whole set by hand as SVG. You get framework components, standalone SVGs, a sprite, CSS for states and dark mode, a review catalog and a README, all validated. 🇧🇷 Em português: uma skill para Claude Code (e outros agentes) que gera uma biblioteca de ícones original no estilo do seu design system. Lê seus tokens e ícones atuais, propõe o estilo, mostra uma amostra dentro da sua UI e só depois desenha tudo. Grátis, licença MIT. What you get • Style matched to your project: grid, stroke or fill, tones, corner radius, states (default, hover, active, disabled), palette per theme.

stories.title: Google Will Make AI Agents Use Its MCP Servers. The Gmail One Can't Send Email
stories.body: From February 2027, Google's terms require AI agents to reach Gmail, Drive and the rest of Workspace through Google's own MCP servers. What the rule says, what the servers can and can't do, and what to change before the deadline.

I open my email inbox, and I find pitches and articles from ostensibly serious people with ostensibly serious credentials attached to ostensibly serious institutions who want to publish things attached to their reputations and mine, and I see Claude .

stories.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
stories.body:
The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features

My comment on The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features — Hacker News. I had a NYT photographer take my picture at my home earlier this year (for a story about Moltbook, oddly enough). At one point I asked if they could fix things up if I had a stain on my shirt and they said absolutely not - they present photographs as they were taken, with cropping and balancing applied but no edits beyond that. He did spend a bunch of time trying to find the best possible natural lighting for the shots he wanted.

stories.title: The Hidden Spiegeltent in Chicago, Illinois
stories.body:
A Belgian mirror tent built inside a forgotten Masonic hall, 14 floors above the Loop.

Spiegeltents were made to travel. These round wooden dance halls, lined with mirrors and stained glass, went from fair to fair. They went up fast and came down fast. The one on Randolph Street is not going anywhere. It was built indoors, on the 14th floor of a Loop building. The building opened in 1926. Rapp & Rapp designed it, with the Oriental Theatre movie palace on the lower floors. The theater is now the James M. Nederlander Theatre. The whole building stands on the site of the Iroquois Theatre, where a fire in 1903 became one of the deadliest in American history.
